explanation.text: For a soy-to-beef-burger flavor gap, the most critical missing meat-like notes are 2-methyl-3-furanthiol and 2-furfurylthiol (meaty/roasted) [1-s2.0-S0963996926007192-main.pdf p.9.0], sulfur-containing furan derivatives [1-s2.0-S0924224421002764-main.pdf p.11.0], Maillard reaction products including pyrazines [foods-12-00923.pdf p.4.0], and free glutamic acid for umami character [1-s2.0-S0924224421002764-main.pdf p.11.0]. Soy's dominant off-notes are beany/green aldehydes — especially hexanal [1-s2.0-S0963996926007192-main.pdf p.1.0] [foods-12-00923.pdf p.2.0] — alongside 1-octen-3-ol [journal.pone.0269278.pdf p.8.0], 2-pentylfuran [fnut-13-1866732.pdf p.12.0], and onion/garlic sulfides (dimethyl disulfide, dimethyl trisulfide) [1-s2.0-S0963996926007192-main.pdf p.8.0]. The top-ranked lever is a D-xylose and L-cysteine Maillard reaction system (0.8% addition, 3:2 ratio), which directly generates 2-methyl-3-furanthiol and 2-furfurylthiol in texturized soy protein [1-s2.0-S0963996926007192-main.pdf p.1.0]. Beany aldehydes can be addressed by beta-cyclodextrin encapsulation [journal.pone.0269278.pdf p.8.0] [Plant_protein_flavor_chemistry_fundamentals_and_te.pdf p.14.0], while lactic acid bacteria fermentation offers additional reduction of hexanal and 2-pentylfuran off-notes [foods-15-00039.pdf p.9.0].
